meta.hypothesis: Flipping RECOMB_BOOST 2.0->1.0 (E7d) shifts the chemistry (slightly more OH) and the cascade (more ionizations), so the SSB indirect/direct ratio could drift out of PARTRAC 2-3. Test: does it hold without recalibrating SSB_P_INDIRECT (which was tuned at 2.0)?
meta.method: Ran tools/run_irt_ssb.cjs (IRT chemistry + indirect SSB via the worker, direct SSB + DSB clustering ported from src/scoring/ssb-dsb.ts) on the RECOMB=1.0 10 keV dump (rad_E10000_recomb1.bin), on a GitHub 16 GB runner (GPU-free). Constants UNCHANGED from production (P_indirect=0.05, P_direct=0.15, r_indirect=1.0).
meta.passBar: indirect/direct ratio stays in PARTRAC [2,3] band without recalibration.

summary.headline: RECOMB->1.0 SSB ratio = 2.32 (was 2.46 @ 2.0) — STILL in PARTRAC 2-3 band, NO P_indirect recalibration needed. The production flip does not break strand-break validation. With E7d (cascade 0.677->0.766x) and E10r (parameter-free chemistry), all three gates pass.

conclusion: RECOMB_BOOST->1.0 is fully validated: cascade ions recover [E7d], chemistry is parameter-free [E10r], SSB ratio holds in band [this]. Production can flip to 1.0 for a parameter-free pipeline.
